title: BMW/MINI Service Advisor
description:
About the role

We have an excellent opportunity available for a motivated Service Advisor to join our team at Sytner BMW/MINI Sheffield.

As a Sytner Service Advisor, you will provide outstanding customer care and be the vital link between our customers and the workshop. You will inform and consult on vehicle servicing, and keep the customer up to date at every stage whilst answering any questions or queries they may have. You will also liaise with technicians/workshop control about vehicle statuses and ensure that vehicles will be ready on time. You will also have the ability to give the best advice on our products and services to our customers.

This is a challenging role where customer care always comes first, you'll take the time to talk to people, build a genuine rapport and identify exactly what our customers want and need.

Sytner Service Advisors work a variety of flexible patterns which can typically include weekends to ensure we provide our customers with the highest possible levels of service.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:

title: Family Legal Secretary - Sheffield
description:
Family Legal Secretary - Sheffield, South Yorkshire Full Time Permanent Competitive Salary + Excellent Benefits

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a motivated and organised Family Legal Secretary to join the established Family Law department of a highly regarded law firm in Sheffield.

This is a fantastic opportunity to become part of one of the UK's largest Family Law teams, providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support to experienced solicitors handling a broad range of family and children law matters.

Previous experience within Family Law, Matrimonial Law or Child Care Law would be advantageous, although applications are also welcomed from experienced Legal Secretaries with a background in other practice areas who are keen to develop their careers in Family Law.

Comprehensive training, ongoing support and genuine opportunities for career progression are available.

The Role Working closely with solicitors and other members of the Family Law team, you will provide comprehensive legal secretarial and administrative support across a varied caseload, including divorce, separation, children matters, care proceedings and financial settlements.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Providing professional and compassionate client care, handling telephone calls, emails and face-to-face enquiries.
- Preparing and formatting legal correspondence, statements and court documentation.
- Producing and organising court bundles for Family Court hearings.
- Audio typing, note taking and general legal document production.
- Managing diaries, appointments and meetings with clients, barristers and other professionals.
- Opening new client files, completing onboarding procedures and maintaining accurate records using the firm's case management system.
- Liaising with solicitors and other legal professionals regarding case progression.
- Keeping clients informed and ensuring enquiries are dealt with promptly and sensitively.
- Maintaining accurate electronic and paper files.
- Handling confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

About You The successful candidate will be an organised, approachable and proactive individual who enjoys working in a busy legal environment and delivering excellent client service.

Ideally, you will have:
- Previous experience as a Legal Secretary, Legal Administrator or Legal Assistant.
- Experience within Family Law, Matrimonial Law or Children Law, although this is not essential.
- Strong audio typing and document production skills.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Experience using legal case management systems.
- The ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively to deadlines.
- A professional, empathetic and discreet approach when dealing with sensitive client matters.

Applications are particularly encouraged from Legal Secretaries who are interested in moving into Family Law and developing specialist knowledge within a supportive department.

Salary & Benefits The firm offers a competitive salary alongside an excellent benefits package, including:
- 23 days' annual leave for support staff, increasing with service to a maximum of 28 days.
- 3 additional discretionary days over Christmas, plus bank holidays.
- Flexible working arrangements, subject to the requirements of the role.
- Flexi-time opportunities and up to 4 additional flex days per year.
- Contributory pension scheme.
- Group Life Assurance after qualifying service.
- Enhanced support through sick pay and contractual maternity pay provisions.
- Excellent training, professional development and internal progression opportunities.
- Employee recognition and referral reward schemes.
- Access to wellbeing initiatives and staff social events.
- Optional benefits including healthcare, Cycle to Work and staff savings schemes.

Apply Now If you are an experienced Legal Secretary, Family Legal Secretary, Matrimonial Legal Secretary or Legal Administrator looking for an opportunity to join a respected and supportive law firm in Sheffield, I would be delighted to hear from you.

Whether you already have Family Law experience or are looking to move into this rewarding area of legal practice, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Please get in touch for a confidential discussion or send your CV to find out more.

title: IP Administrator (Experienced)
description:
IP Administrator (Experienced)
Sheffield

About Us

Withers & Rogers is one of Europe's largest dedicated intellectual property law firms, with offices across the UK, Paris and Munich. Established more than 140 years ago, we remain as passionate as ever about making intellectual property work to our clients' best advantage. Today, our clients include many renowned, innovative organisations from across Europe, North America, and Asia.

We believe that our patent and trade mark attorneys, support, and operations staff have a breadth of expertise and a depth of specialist sector knowledge that is second to none. Our purpose is building trusting relationships, and our vision is to be an independent, responsible, sustainably profitable, and globally focused firm.

The Role

This is a full-time, permanent position, and the successful candidate will be aligned to our Sheffield office. Hybrid working options, including working from home, are available.

In this role, your responsibilities will include:
- Managing own and team inboxes, processing emails and post (mainly electronic but some hard copy), updating our case management system and acknowledging receipt, where appropriate.
- Accurate and daily maintenance of the case management system, including following workflows and generating standard correspondence from templates, and liaising with Records and Finance departments, as well as sister company Withers & Rogers Renewals.
- Full secretarial support, including all typing of documents such as letters, emails, and patent specifications.
- Preparation of official forms for UK, European and other patent applications, and design applications, including use of online filing software, the payment of official fees and reporting accurately.
- Organising and prioritising own workload and keeping a level-headed approach in a busy working environment.
- Accurately following Withers & Rogers processes and procedures, and client-specific processes and procedures where applicable.
- Producing/maintaining documentation to capture processes developed for key clients.
- Accurate preparation and processing of invoices, using e-billing systems where necessary.

About You

To join us as an IP Administrator, you'll need:
- Patent administration experience is required.
- Good communication skills and ability to interact with all levels of internal and external contacts.
- Attention to detail and pride in work product.
- The ability to balance and prioritise workload, remain composed and level-headed during periods of particularly busy activity, and proactively help other members of the team.
- The ability to manage an attorney's emails, judge urgency, and act as required.
- Good Microsoft package skills, particularly Outlook, Word, Teams and Excel, with ideally an understanding of case management systems and experience in following/generating standard procedures and templates for repeat tasks.
- The desire to learn and a willingness to become involved.
- The ability to work individually and within a team.

Your Rewards
- Competitive salary
- Benefits such as a healthcare cash plan and an additional holiday purchase scheme
- Flexible working options
- Enhanced Parental Leave options
- Positive and welcoming work environment

Applications will be reviewed as they are received, so early applications are encouraged.

We foster a supportive and inclusive culture where employees are encouraged to broaden their knowledge, challenge themselves and share their ideas.

If you think you have the skills to succeed, we would love to hear from you.

title: Litigation Paralegal
description:
Role: Litigation Paralegal
Location: Sheffield, South Yorkshire
Contract: Full time, permanent
Salary: £23,000 - £27,000

As a Litigation Paralegal within this established in-house legal team, you will play a vital role in managing legal recovery claims relating to commercial property and infrastructure damage. Working within a structured, high-volume environment, your duties will include:
- Monitoring Incoming Claims: Regularly review and assess new damage claims submitted by external stakeholders, contractors, or third parties, ensuring accuracy and completeness of information.
- Case Management: Handle a personal caseload of legal recovery files from initial instruction through to final resolution. Use internal systems to track progress, maintain documentation, and ensure compliance with service level agreements.
- Claim Evaluation & Qualification: Conduct early-stage analysis of claims to determine liability, legal merit, and potential recovery value. Ensure cases meet the required thresholds for progressing to litigation where necessary.
- Negotiation & Settlement: Engage with third parties, insurers, and legal representatives to negotiate out-of-court settlements wherever possible, while protecting the organisation's commercial interests.
- Litigation Support: Where disputes cannot be resolved through negotiation, prepare case files for formal legal proceedings. This includes drafting pleadings, witness statements, and other relevant legal documents.
- Evidence Gathering: Undertake detailed investigative work by analysing technical documents, reviewing planning maps and diagrams, and liaising with internal operational teams to gather essential case facts.
- Client Liaison & Stakeholder Communication: Maintain regular contact with internal departments and external parties, including engineers, surveyors, contractors, and claims specialists, to ensure consistent information flow throughout the claims process.
- Compliance & Risk Awareness: Ensure that all casework is conducted in line with relevant legislation, regulatory standards, and internal policy. Proactively flag potential legal risks or anomalies to supervising solicitors.
- Use of Case Management Systems: Utilise specialist case management software to manage documentation, record actions, and produce reports. Contribute to data accuracy and overall operational efficiency.

Candidate Profile:

To be considered for this role, applicants must have:
- Previous experience in a legal setting
- Exposure to civil or commercial litigation
- The ability to handle a high volume of cases with efficiency and accuracy

How to apply:

- CRA Legal follow strict best practice recruitment guidelines monitored by the Recruitment and Employment Confederation (REC). Please note our advertisements use salary levels purely as a guide. However we are happy to consider applications from all candidates who are able to demonstrate the skills necessary to fulfil the role.
- This vacancy is very popular with the local legal community, so please apply quickly to ensure your application is considered. As part of our candidate registration and care process we at CRA Legal aim to respond to all successful applications within 2 working days.

title: Personal Injury Legal Assistant
description:
Role: Personal Injury Legal Assistant
Location: Sheffield, South Yorkshire
Contract: Full time, permanent
Salary: £24,000 - £26,000

CRA Consulting is pleased to be working alongside a leading claimant law firm in Sheffield to recruit a Personal Injury Legal Assistant to join its growing team.

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience in Personal Injury, legal administration or paralegal work who is looking to develop their technical knowledge and take on greater responsibility within a busy claimant environment.
The role will initially involve supporting the team across a range of Personal Injury matters, with the opportunity to transition into Data Breach and GDPR-related claims as your experience develops.

The Role
As a Legal Assistant, you will be hands-on with live matters and closely involved in progressing claims from initial instruction through to resolution. You'll work alongside experienced fee earners and solicitors, gaining exposure to the wider claims process and taking on increasing responsibility as you develop.
Your duties will include:
- Assisting with the day-to-day progression of Personal Injury claims
- Liaising with clients, insurers, medical professionals and other third parties
- Preparing and reviewing legal documentation and correspondence
- Obtaining and reviewing supporting evidence and medical records
- Assisting with drafting statements and other case documentation
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date case records
- Managing key dates, deadlines and ongoing case actions
- Supporting fee earners with the progression of litigated and pre-litigation matters
- Developing an understanding of Data Breach and GDPR claims, with a view to transitioning into this area of work
- Taking on increased responsibility for your own caseload as your knowledge and confidence develops

Progression into Data Breach
A key part of the opportunity is the genuine progression into Data Breach work.
You'll receive support and training to develop your understanding of claims arising from data breaches and GDPR infringements, including the impact these incidents can have on individuals. The Legal Assistants within the team are very involved in the progression of matters, so this is much more than a traditional administrative support role.

Over time, there is the opportunity to take on more responsibility and develop your own expertise within this specialist area.
About You
The firm is open to candidates from a range of backgrounds, but you are likely to have:
- Previous experience within a legal environment
- Ideally, some exposure to Personal Injury, claimant work or litigation
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to manage a busy workload and work to deadlines
- A genuine interest in developing your legal knowledge and taking on greater responsibility
- A proactive and client-focused approach

This could suit an experienced Legal Assistant, Paralegal or Personal Injury support professional who is looking for a role offering hands-on experience, specialist training and genuine career progression.
The Opportunity

You'll be joining an established team in Sheffield with the opportunity to build on your existing legal experience and develop specialist knowledge in an area of growing importance.
For the right person, this role offers a clear route from Personal Injury Legal Assistant into specialist Data Breach work, with increasing responsibility and opportunities to progress within the team.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Purchase Ledger Clerk
Sheffield - Full Time, Permanent (Hybrid Working)

We're looking for an experienced Purchase Ledger Clerk to join a leading organisation, based in Sheffield to support their busy finance team and take ownership of the day-to-day purchase ledger process, whilst also supporting with a wider range of transactional finance activities.

This is a great role for someone who enjoys the detail and accuracy that comes with Purchase Ledger, but doesn't want to be limited in their responsibilities. You'll become an important part of the team, working closely with colleagues across the business and getting involved in different areas as you develop.

Duties will include:
- Processing and coding purchase invoices
- Matching invoices to purchase orders and delivery notes
- Setting up and maintaining supplier accounts
- Completing supplier statement reconciliations
- Managing supplier queries and resolving invoice discrepancies
- Preparing and assisting with payment runs
- Ensuring the purchase ledger is accurate and up to date
- Supporting month-end activities and reconciliations
- Assisting with wider transactional finance duties across the team
- Providing support with general finance administration and ad-hoc finance tasks

We're looking for someone who already has Purchase Ledger experience and understands the importance of accuracy, organisation and keeping on top of deadlines.

You'll be comfortable dealing with suppliers, able to investigate and resolve queries and confident working through a high volume of invoices where required. Just as importantly, you'll be someone who enjoys being part of a team and is happy to get involved outside of your core responsibilities.

This would suit someone who is looking for a varied transactional finance role, where they can use their existing Purchase Ledger experience whilst continuing to broaden their knowledge across finance.

title: Reception Administrator
description: This role is at the heart of our organisations day-to-day operations. As the first point of contact for many of our clients, visitors, and team members, youll play a vital part in creating a welcoming, professional, and efficient environment. We created this role to support our growing need for reliable, organised, and people-focused administrative support. Youll be joining a team that values collaboration, empowerment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. Your work will help ensure that our front-of-house experience reflects the high standards we set across all our services. From managing enquiries and coordinating appointments to supporting internal processes, youll be instrumental in keeping things running smoothly and helping others do their best work. We provide the tools and support individuals need to challenge themselves and push their recovery to its fullest potential, empowering them not only to recover but to thrive. As a Reception Administrator at STEPS, you will provide the first point of contact for STEPS clients, visitors, external organisations and suppliers as well as providing vital administrative support for our service. You will work as part of a wider inter-disciplinary team with collective responsibility for delivering first-class service in rehabilitative care aligned with STEPS values and behaviours. We know that exceptional care begins with exceptional people. Thats why weve built a specialist interdisciplinary team, who bring not only skill and experience, but real compassion to every interaction. We employ 180+ team members in both clinical positions and in business support roles and we are proud of the culture we have established where all team members share our philosophy, values and dedication to delivering excellent client care. Our team is united by a common purpose, dedicated to continually learning from one another, and committed to giving their utmost for those we support. We invest and nurture the development of our team, and through training, shared learning, and research, we give them the tools to grow, stay inspired, and remain at the forefront of their area of work. This Job description is an outline which reflects the present requirements of the post and is not intended to be exhaustive list of duties the post holder will be expected to fulfil. To provide a professional, courteous and prompt first point of contact for clients, visiting families, guests and external visitors. To be responsible for providing a client-centred reception service which; - Deals with all enquiries appropriately, referring issues which cannot be resolved immediately by referring to the correct team member - Maintains appropriate call and action logs - Ensures that the correct processes are followed for client and guest sign in and sign out, including making sure people are aware of the correct site safety procedures - Carries out all start and end of day processes for reception - Ensures that the reception area and the admin office is kept tidy and presentable at all times - Takes delivery and sign for packages and post - Takes cash/card payments from clients and team members when necessary - Books taxis for clients and visitors when requested or agreed by a STEPS team member according to the relevant procedures To provide additional administrative support as appropriate, for example; - Typing up clinical notes as required - Input client timetables - Raise Invoices - Order clinical supplies, stationery and other equipment as requested To comply with STEPS policies and procedures at all times To maintain client confidentiality at all times whilst carrying out duties. To ensure confidentiality of information in respect of records maintained and tasks undertaken To undertake any other duties which may be specified from time to time by Head of Admin that are within the level and responsibility appropriate to the post To effectively communicate using a variety of styles that demonstrates the values and behaviours of STEPS. To communicate with people clearly and in a manner and at a level and pace appropriate to their abilities, preferences and beliefs. To be respectful of a clients dignity at all times and develop effective relationships with clients, their families, carers, the interdisciplinary team.
